title: Rainbow after a monsoon shower
body: After a monsoon shower, Riya sees a rainbow in the evening sky while the Sun is setting behind her. Her teacher explains that the air is still full of tiny water droplets. Each droplet behaves like a small prism. Sunlight entering a droplet is refracted and split into its colours. The light then strikes the back surface of the droplet and is reflected internally, and it is refracted again as it comes out of the droplet. Because different colours bend through different angles, they leave the droplets in slightly different directions, and different colours reach Riya's eyes from different droplets. The teacher adds that a rainbow is always formed in the direction opposite to the Sun, and that a similar band of colours can be seen in the spray of a waterfall or a fountain when the Sun is behind the observer.
